comparator.name: Communication and Life Sciences (Bachelor Communicatie en Life Sciences)
comparator.academicYear: Latest complete official WUR curriculum: 2025–2026, checked 2026-09-28
comparator.sourceNotes: The latest complete official study-handbook structure available for BCL is 2025–2026; the 2026–2027 API currently returns no study object, while current WUR programme, admissions and 2026–2027 graduation material still identify BCL. The 180-EC reconstruction therefore uses the complete 2025–2026 handbook: 105 EC of compulsory named courses, a 15-EC thesis and 60 EC of elective space, including 24 EC in a chosen life-science domain.

alternatives.label: Communication, media & societal change
alternatives.concept: A closest feasible liberal-arts pathway in communication, media, persuasion and societal change, supported by politics, sociology, psychology and quantitative and qualitative research methods.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines rhetoric, persuasion, media analysis, politics, sociology, social psychology and empirical methods; the broad label does not imply a dedicated life-science communication sequence.
progression: Communication and media introductions precede advanced persuasion, documentary, organisational and applied communication study; social-science and data foundations precede advanced methods. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with six 300-level courses.

alternatives.label: Health communication & behaviour
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme combines public health, physiology, disease, health and social psychology with a six-course communication and media sequence and empirical methods.
alternatives.concept: Builds the evidenced Health direction around public health, behaviour, disease, psychology, ethics and communication design so students can analyse how health knowledge and interventions are communicated.
progression: Life-science, public-health, psychology, communication, data and research foundations precede advanced health psychology, disease study, persuasion and applied communication. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with seven 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes health, disease, behaviour and public-health evidence the application domain for communication. It differs from the closest communication-and-media programme by well over four courses and 30 EC.

alternatives.label: Sustainability, climate & environmental communication
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme visibly combines climate, earth systems, environmental governance and sustainability research with a six-course communication and media sequence.
alternatives.concept: Builds the evidenced Sustainability and Climate Change directions around climate and earth systems, environmental governance and applied sustainability research, with communication, persuasion and media study as the public-engagement strand.
progression: Sustainability, communication, media, data and earth-system foundations precede environmental law, public economics, applied environmental research, governance and advanced persuasion. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass, with eight 300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes climate, earth systems and sustainability governance the application domain for communication. It differs from both other programmes by well over four courses and 30 EC.

core: Communication theory, rhetoric, persuasion, media and communication processes
Communication, power, politics, organisations and social change
Life-science and health domains for communication
Sustainability, climate, food, agriculture, natural resources and urban domains for communication
Qualitative, quantitative, intervention-design and independent communication research
adjacent: Media, persuasion and communication for societal change
Communication in food, agriculture, natural resources and urbanisation
questions: How can communication connect expert knowledge, public understanding and social action?
How do rhetoric, media and institutions shape public debate and social change?
How can communication and behavioural evidence improve health interventions?
How can communication support climate and sustainability transitions?

candidates.label: Food and agricultural communication
candidates.reason: Food and agriculture are valid application domains, but the three-alternative maximum is reached; communication design and sustainability content already provide partial substantive coverage.

candidates.label: Natural-resource communication
candidates.reason: This is a valid application domain, but the three-alternative maximum is reached and the environmental-communication programme already covers natural-resource governance and public engagement.

candidates.label: Urban communication
candidates.reason: This is a valid application domain, but the three-alternative maximum is reached; it would not justify replacing either of the more strongly evidenced included application directions.

selection.assessment: The closest programme captures communication, media and societal change. Health and sustainability/climate support two coherent, feasible and pairwise-distinct application directions. Production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: WUR offers a dedicated communication-science curriculum integrated with life-science application study and a communication thesis. UCR can combine rhetoric, media, persuasion, social research and substantive health or environmental study, but it does not reproduce the same communication-science methods sequence or required life-science domain structure.
